facts.fact: The Caafimaad+ Digitalized Data System is run by the CaafimaadPlus consortium of ten NGOs, which describes itself as partnering with the Federal Ministry of Health rather than handing the system to it (April 2026).
The consortium states the system is funded by EU Humanitarian Aid (ECHO); no government budget contribution is mentioned (April 2026).

The consortium reports the system operational in over 40 facilities across 9 regions and more than 25 districts of South-Central Somalia, capturing over 3,000 consultations a day; it gives no denominator and does not say what tier the facilities are, though it names a maternal health clinic and health posts (April 2026).

The consortium says the system replaces manual reports with real-time entry, lets a nurse call up a patient's history instantly and makes a family's record available at any facility on the system (April 2026).
The consortium reports growth from a five-facility pilot in mid-2024 to over 40 facilities by April 2026; it does not date the steps in between.

systems.owner: CaafimaadPlus consortium (Action Against Hunger, Concern Worldwide, Trocaire, International Medical Corps and six others), funded by ECHO
systems.tiers: over 40 facilities in 9 regions and 25+ districts of South-Central Somalia; a maternal health clinic and health posts named

systems.owner: International Medical Corps, within the CaafimaadPlus consortium
systems.tiers: consortium-supported facilities; handheld devices and barcode scanning at dispensing

note: C+ DDS is classed emr on what the document says it does: it holds a family's health record, retrievable at another facility, across health, nutrition, WASH and protection consultations. It also pushes data into the ministry's DHIS2 in real time, but the document does not say what DHIS2 does, so no hmis fact is taken. The count is stated as over 40, recorded as 40. The body is repeated three times in the file.
